title: UK labour market overview — earnings, unemployment and vacancies (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET), the D-2 print the December MPC does read — two 2026 non-Report rounds already incorporated a same-morning labour bulletin
source: EST: two UK-government primaries fetched direct 2026-09-09, both HTTP 200. (1) ons.gov.uk/releases/uklabourmarketdecember2026 — the ONS release-calendar entry reads 'UK Labour Market: December 2026', '15 December 2026 7:00am', 'Estimates of employment, unemployment, inactivity, average weekly earnings, vacancies and other labour market related statistics for the UK', marked 'This release is not yet published.' (2) gov.uk/government/statistics/announcements/uk-labour-market-december-2026 — the statutory pre-announcement register reads '15 December 2026 7:00am (confirmed)', producer Office for National Statistics, designation 'Accredited official statistics'. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts carries BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS:/FED: and has no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics — the same gap uk-labour-market-2026-09-15, uk-labour-market-2026-10-20 and uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 were filed under. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Proposed 2026-09-09 by the uk-labour-market-2026-11-17 lane; researched and made canonical by its own lane the same day
notes: RESEARCHED 2026-09-09 by its own lane (docs/research/events/uk-labour-market-2026-12-15.md), which read the single proposal in full and re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting it. The proposal it supersedes — proposals/uk-labour-market-2026-12-15.from-uk-labour-market-2026-11-17.json — is now inert and stays where it is. THREE FINDINGS, AND THE FIRST CORRECTS A SIBLING'S RECORD. (1) A SIBLING LANE'S NEGATIVE WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE, AND IT IS DATED. boe-decision-2026-12-17's canonical notes state, of the same 2026-09-09: 'The December UK labour-market date is NOT yet announced (gov.uk statistics announcements, fetched 2026-09-09: zero results in the December-2026 window) and is deliberately NOT proposed.' The gov.uk register page exists at the conventional slug and reads '15 December 2026 7:00am (confirmed)' — re-fetched today at HTTP 200. That lane declined to file on a SEARCH-ENUMERATION failure, not an absence, and the consequence is substantive: its ledger frames the December vote's run-in as 'THE RUN-IN IS ONE DAY' (UK CPI 12-16 alone). The run-in is TWO days and this print is the FIRST of them — 53 hours to the 12:00 London announcement against CPI's 29. The general rule the miss teaches: a null from a search index is not a primary negative; the direct publisher slug is. (2) THE D-2 PLACEMENT QUESTION THE 11-17 LANE LEFT OPEN HAS A DOCUMENTED PRECEDENT, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN D-2. That lane registered FT-uk-labour-market-2026-11-17-3 because 'whether a D-2 release is inside a non-Report round's briefing set is a question no primary settled today'. Two 2026 non-Report rounds settle it a fortiori, both fetched today: the March round announced 2026-03-19 12:00 and the ONS bulletin released 2026-03-19 — the SAME MORNING — and the minutes cite 'annual growth in private sector regular Average Weekly Earnings in the three months to January had been 3.3%' and 'The Labour Force Survey unemployment rate had been 5.2% in the three months to January', which are that bulletin's own Nov-2025-to-Jan-2026 windows and figures; the June round announced 2026-06-18 12:00, the ONS bulletin released 2026-06-18, and the minutes cite private regular AWE 'in the three months to April had been 2.9%', the bulletin's own Feb-Apr figure. A print published five hours before the vote reached both sets of minutes; a print published 53 hours before this one is not the marginal case. The March minutes also date the distinction that matters: their stated cut-off, '16 March 2026', is for ENERGY-PRICE conditioning assumptions, not for official data releases. (3) THE PROPOSAL'S BUDGET CLAIM IS REFUTED ON ITS OWN ARITHMETIC. It reads 'the first labour reference window that is wholly after the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget'. Rolling the publication pattern forward — corroborated across THREE bulletins fetched today, each carrying the three months ending two months before its release month (March 2026 release: Nov-Jan; June: Feb-Apr; August: Apr-Jun) — puts this release at Aug-Oct AWE/LFS, Sep-Nov vacancies, November payroll flash. Aug-Oct 2026 is not wholly after 2026-10-28: two of its three months close entirely before Budget day and the third contains three post-Budget days. The November payrolled-employees flash IS wholly post-Budget and is the only cell that qualifies — and per the 11-17 lane's April-lag precedent (Autumn Budget 2024-10-30 raised secondary Class 1 NICs 13.8%->15% effective April 2025) no Budget wage response is observable in this print either way. WHAT THE WINDOW ACTUALLY IS: Aug-Oct straddles UPWARD — two months in 2026 Q3, which the July MPR puts at around 3.0% private-sector AWE (search-relayed), and one month in Q4, for which NO private-AWE path is published anywhere findable today (the July MPR page and PDF were checked). So the 11-17 lane's tightened >=3.3% kill cannot be carried forward: its cause was a window that did not straddle, and this one does, against an unanchored third. Re-derived, not inherited, at >=3.4%, with the 2026-11-05 Monetary Policy Report named as the event that gives the Q4 third an anchor and should replace the tolerance with arithmetic. IMPACT LOW, argued not inherited: symbols [], this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol, no house playbook is rates- or sterling-keyed, and the measured cable reaction to the 2026-08-18 release was ~0.1% on a two-sided beat. ATTRIBUTION IS THE WORST OF THE FOUR UK LABOUR ENTRIES: 36 tracked events sit within five days, this print shares its morning with ppi-2026-12-15 and empire-state-mfg-2026-12-15 (both 08:30 ET, 6.5 hours later), it lands inside quarterly-opex week (opex-2026-12-18) and on day 4 of a possible US federal funding lapse (cr-expiry-2026-12-11 / government-funding-deadline-2026-12-11), with fomc-2026-12-09 six days behind, ecb-decision-2026-12-17 75 minutes after the BoE on the same day, and boj-decision-2026-12-18 the day after. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
